summary: Root cause identified: a bug introduced in order-service v2.15.2 malformed the request to exchange-gateway, leading to 504 Gateway Timeout errors and a 30% order failure rate. Confidence is medium (60%) based on strong supporting observations. Immediate rollback mitigates impact while a fix is prepared.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bug introduced in order-service v2.15.2 causing exchange-gateway timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The order-service deployment v2.15.2 introduced a code bug that malformed the request to exchange‑gateway, causing the gateway to return 504 Gateway Timeout responses. Order‑service logs the failure, leading to a sharp latency increase and a 30 % error rate.

causal_chain.claim: new code sends malformed or mis‑routed request to exchange‑gateway
order-service logs "exchange‑gateway call failed: 504" and returns 504 to callers
order-service latency spikes (p99 >5 s) and error rate climbs to ~33 %

assumptions: The malformed request is the direct cause of the 504 response (not a downstream issue).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Exchange‑gateway internal failure returning 504 errors
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A failure inside exchange‑gateway (e.g., overload or internal error) caused it to return 504 Gateway Timeout responses to order‑service, which then propagated the failures to callers.

causal_chain.claim: exchange‑gateway experiences internal issue causing 504 responses
order‑service logs the failure and returns 504 to callers
order‑service latency spikes and error rate rises

assumptions: exchange‑gateway can emit 504 responses without logging an explicit error.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Network connectivity issue between order‑service and exchange‑gateway
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A transient network or routing problem between order‑service and exchange‑gateway caused requests to time out, resulting in 504 errors observed by order‑service.

causal_chain.claim: Network path between order‑service and exchange‑gateway degrades (packet loss / latency)
order‑service requests to exchange‑gateway time out, yielding 504 responses
order‑service logs the timeout and returns 504 to callers
order‑service latency spikes and error rate climbs

assumptions: No other services observed the same network issue (lack of data).

facts.statement: order-service version v2.15.2 was deployed at 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z and rolled back at 2026-03-17T11:16:00Z.
The first ERROR log in order-service appears at 2026-03-17T11:02:45Z, after the deployment.
All early ERROR logs share the signature "exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)".
No ERROR logs are present in order-service before 2026-03-17T11:02:45Z.
Order-service p99 latency spiked from ~150 ms to >5 s at 2026-03-17T11:01:00Z.
Order-service error rate jumped from <0.3% to >15% at 2026-03-17T11:01:00Z and rose to ~33% by 11:15.
Order-service request rate remained stable (~220‑240 req/s) during the incident window.
Exchange-gateway logs contain zero ERROR entries with "Gateway Timeout" between 11:00 and 12:30 UTC.
Payment-service shows zero ERROR logs containing "Gateway Timeout" between 11:00 and 12:00 UTC.

assumptions: The malformed request generated by the new order-service code is the direct cause of the 504 responses (i.e., exchange-gateway does not treat a well‑formed request as an error).
Exchange-gateway would emit ERROR logs if it experienced an internal failure that produced 504 responses.

timeline.event: Order-service p99 latency spikes and error rate begins to rise.
First ERROR log appears in order-service, indicating exchange-gateway 504 failures.
Error rate reaches ~33%; latency remains >5 s.
Rollback of order-service to previous version (v2.15.1) initiated.

recommended_actions.action: Rollback order-service to version v2.15.1 (or the last known good version).
recommended_actions.rationale: Restores correct request format to exchange-gateway, eliminating 504 errors and reducing error rate.

recommended_actions.action: Patch order-service v2.15.2 to correct the request formatting bug and redeploy after verification.
recommended_actions.rationale: Fixes the root cause while allowing the new version to be used after validation.

recommended_actions.action: Add unit/integration tests that validate the request payload sent to exchange-gateway, ensuring proper formatting.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents regression of this bug in future releases.

recommended_actions.action: Enhance observability: collect latency and error metrics from exchange-gateway, pricing-engine, and kafka; ensure inventory-service logs are searchable.
recommended_actions.rationale: Reduces data gaps that limited root‑cause confidence and improves future incident detection.

data_gaps: Missing logs from inventory-service due to unknown service name, preventing correlation of potential downstream errors.
No DB connection usage metrics for ledger-db, limiting ability to rule out DB saturation as a cause of 504 responses.
Absence of downstream latency and error metrics (pricing-engine, exchange-gateway, kafka) hampers full verification that the issue was isolated to order-service request formatting.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: If exchange-gateway logs later show internal errors or overload conditions coinciding with the 504 responses, hypothesis H2 (dependency failure) would become more plausible.
If network trace data revealed packet loss or routing failures between order-service and exchange-gateway during the incident window, hypothesis H3 (network issue) would gain support.
Discovery of a malformed request pattern that existed prior to the v2.15.2 deployment would weaken the link between the deployment and the failures.

findings.statement: A deployment of order-service version v2.15.2 was applied at 2026-03-17T10:48:00Z and rolled back at 2026-03-17T11:16:00Z.
No other services had code deployments in the 6‑hour window (05:10–12:59 UTC).
A configuration change on pricing-engine altered cache.ttl_seconds from 5 to 4 at 2026-03-17T09:20:00Z.
No other configuration or feature‑flag changes were recorded for any service in the same window.
order-service calls four downstream components: ledger-db (Postgres), pricing-engine (HTTP), exchange-gateway (HTTP), and kafka (queue produce).
order-service receives traffic from api-gateway (HTTP) and shares the ledger-db, redis-cache, and kafka datastores with other services.
